inputs: REQ-3's rows file and summary (the pools s3_safe and s3_orig listed with the SHA-256s that REQ-6's and REQ-9's records name); REQ-6's s_pool_record.json; REQ-9's untuned_answers_record.json; each by SHA-256
name: score_s3_datarx
next: write_score_add.py (scorer s3) selects the top 48; write_add_edit.py (list s3) writes the add edit
reports: S1's SAS; |S1 & S3 subset|; the share of the subset's y^orig that the lexicon calls REFUSAL-OPENING; the capped count; the ids leaving the ranking by encode_train's reason; per-layer s^l of both responses, so the scores can be recomputed
requirement: REQ-11 (brief rev 1; RS B8; SPEC sections 3.4-3.6); lead decisions L10, L14 (1); the lead's Part C requirement (model-agnostic)
rule: h^l = read (a) at hidden-state indices l = 1..n (the embedding output excluded; index n = model.norm of the last block's output, L4); s^l(d) = cos(h^l, C_r^l) - cos(h^l, C_c^l) with C_r = the 64 safe anchors' mean and C_c = the 64 harmful anchors' mean (REQ-3's cos_safe - cos_harmful); R(d) = the mean over l; SAS(x) = R(x, y^safe) - R(x, y^orig); only the S3 subset (1,000) is ranked; a y^orig that encode_train refused leaves the ranking and is counted (L14 (1)); S1's 48 rows get their SAS reported (L10 (2))
